summary: FsQuint owns generic ITF values/decoding, deterministic schema-v1 replay and first-divergence comparison, independently of SDD/Coordination domain logic. Raw Itf defaults are 16 MiB, depth64, 10000 states and 100000 collection elements; Replay callbacks initialize/apply/observe/cleanup real consumer state, with expected states kept outside callbacks. Replay timeout/cancellation is cooperative and cleanup receives a fresh uncancelled token; this is not hard containment of an untrusted/noncooperative driver. FsQuint.Tooling is optional, caller-provisioned, digest/version-selected Linux x64 Quint0.32.0 execution for typecheck/test/run only, with no verifier claim. Public stable 0.1.0 extraction and downstream migration are historical accepted evidence; current protected source selects 0.1.1/FSharp.Core10.1.401, which is a separate source identity rather than proof of a new published version. Consumers must require Equivalent together with no CleanupFailure; a cleanup failure is preserved separately rather than changing the original replay outcome. Initialize owns disposal when it fails before returning a runtime.
title: Independent bounded decoding and cooperative replay
